unit.title: Myth, Epic & Archetype
unit.essential_question: How do cultures use stories to examine duty, identity, power, belonging, and the unknown?
big_ideas: A recurring pattern becomes meaningful only inside a particular cultural and historical context.
Heroes reveal communal ideals through their choices, limits, relationships, and consequences.
Comparison should preserve meaningful difference rather than flatten traditions into a universal formula.
Translations and editions are interpretations with identifiable makers, dates, purposes, and limits.
unit.readiness_note: Unit 1 close-reading and evidence practices remain active. Complete Unit 1 or use its skill review before beginning the major comparison.

lessons.title: Why Humans Make Myths
objectives: Distinguish myth as a literary and cultural category from falsehood
Analyze motif, symbol, structure, and cultural function
Record source, tradition, teller or author, translator, edition, and access status

lessons.title: Epic Heroes & Cultural Values
objectives: Analyze how an epic hero embodies and challenges communal ideals
Compare tests, choices, consequences, and relationships
Use tense and voice purposefully in literary analysis

lessons.title: Comparative Myth Synthesis
objectives: Develop a comparative thesis based on a meaningful criterion
Synthesize similarities and differences without erasing context
Revise and defend a comparative literary analysis

required_sources.minimum: Two authentic traditions represented through named, lawful editions; at least one sustained passage from each.
required_sources.edition_rule: Every quotation records work, tradition or author, translator/editor when applicable, edition or host, and location marker.
required_sources.summary_rule: Course and ARSHIF summaries provide orientation only and may not replace the assigned primary passage as literary evidence.

tools.evidence_policy: Machine output is an unreviewed draft and is not authoritative literary evidence.

tools.evidence_policy: English 9 verifies the actual edition used.
